findings.text: root_path is put into a regex unescaped, so regex metacharacters in it are interpreted. For example, root_path '/api(' raises re.error, and root_path '/a.c' also strips '/abc'. Use re.escape, or better, a literal prefix check.

The prefix is stripped without checking a path boundary, and an empty root_path is handled only by accident. With root_path '/app' and path '/application/x', the result is 'lication/x'. If the path doesn't start with root_path, it is returned unchanged, which is silently wrong. Strip only when path == root_path or path starts with root_path + '/'.
Importing starlette.types at module level in _utils may create a circular import, because starlette.types or its dependencies could import _utils. Use a TYPE_CHECKING import.
